sentences.text: 1. Mentioned.
Not on Board.
Taken on Board.
2. Mr. Kamat, Ld.
Counsel appearing on behalf of the Plaintiff has informed the Court that there is no valid/active caveat against the arrest of the Defendant Vessel in the caveat warrant book.
The caveat book is produced and so is a praecipe with an endorsement from the Execution Department that there are no valid 501-jol-17871-2024.doc caveats as on 12th June, 2024.
3. The above Judge's Order has been moved ex-parte after production was granted to the Plaintiff.
The urgent relief sought is the arrest of Defendant No.1 Vessel which is under the ownership of Defendant No.2.

The Suit has been filed for a decree in favour of the Plaintiff against Defendants for a sum of USD 108,012 (i.e. INR 91,32,773.16) as compensation for loss of life-death in service, along with outstanding wages of USD 133.33 (i.e. Rs. 11,136) payable under the Employment Agreement and legal costs of Rs. 5,00,000, along with interest at the rate of 15% p.a. or at such other rate as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit from 31.08.2022 till payment or realization.

Relief is also sought that Kavita Devi vs Mt Dharma on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38843984/
1 the Defendant Vessel be sold under the orders and directions of this Court and the sale proceeds thereof be applied towards the satisfaction of the Plaintiff's claim in the Suit.

sentences.text: It is the case of the Plaintiff that the present Suit has been filed for recovery of compensation towards loss of life of Gulshan Mehra, death during service, outstanding wages/emoluments compensation and other ancillary reliefs.

The Plaintiff is the mother of Gulshan Mehra (since deceased) who was employed by Defendant No.2 as Able-Bodied Seaman, assigned to 501-jol-17871-2024.doc work on MV Asso, but died on 31.08.2022, during his service with Defendants.

The Plaintiff's claim is a maritime claim under Section 4(1)(e) and Section 4(1)(o) and a maritime lien under Section 9(1)
(a) and Section 9(1)(b) of the Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017.

sentences.text: 5. I have heard Mr. Kamat, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Plaintiff and considered the averments made in the Plaint.
On going through the Plaint and the annexures thereto, I find that a prima facie case for arrest of Defendant No.1 Vessel is made out.

The claim in the present Suit is a maritime claim under Section 4(1)(e) and Section 4(1)(o) and a maritime lien under Section 9(1)
(a) and Section 9(1)(b) of the Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017.

sentences.text: The vessel is liable to be arrested under Section 5(1)(a) of the Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017.

entities.text: Admiralty (Jurisdiction and Settlement of Maritime Claims) Act, 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: I also find that the balance of convenience lies in favour of the Plaintiff to whom irreversible prejudice would be caused if the reliefs sought in the Judge's Order were to be denied.

6. In view of the facts averted to earlier, I find that there is a cause of action in favour of the Plaintiff and that the Defendant Vessel being at the port and harbour of Mumbai Port, i.e. within the 501-jol-17871-2024.doc admiralty jurisdiction of the Court.

In these circumstances, I order and direct the arrest of the Defendant Vessel MT Dharma (IMO NO. 9454149), along with her hull,
tackle, engines, machinery, boats, bunkers, equipment, paraphernalia and other appurtenances presently at the port and harbour of Mumbai Port, or wherever she is within the territorial waters of India until the satisfaction of the Plaintiff's claim.
7. I have seen the Judge's Order and it seems to be in a proper form and with the appropriate contents.
I accept the undertakings contained in the Judge's Order as undertakings to the Court.

I,
therefore, make an order in terms of the Judge's Order.
8. All concerned including the port and customs authorities will act upon a copy of this order digitally signed by the Private Secretary/ Personal Assistant of this Court.

9. The Plaintiff is at liberty to forward a copy of a communication from the Sheriff of Mumbai forwarding the digitally signed copy of this order or an authenticated copy of this order, by fax/email/hand delivery/ RPAD to all the concerned authorities.
